transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you into the clinic today?
I keep thinking my wife and the kids would be better off if I just didn’t wake up. I’ve been saying I don’t need to see another winter.
I'm really sorry to hear that you've been feeling this way. How long have these thoughts and feelings been going on?
Since my bowling partner died… about a year and a month ago. That’s when it really started.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in activities you used to enjoy, like bowling?
Yes. I used to look forward to bridge, working in the garden, cooking at church, Cubs games... now I just sit in my chair. I can’t seem to make myself care about any of it.
Before this past year, have you ever experienced a period of feeling this depressed?
I’m not sure. I’ve had hard times, of course, but nothing I can put my finger on like this.
Have you ever had a period where you felt unusually energetic or on top of the world, needing very little sleep?
No, I don’t think so. I can’t recall ever having a spell like that—being unusually energetic or getting by on hardly any sleep.
How has your sleep been during this past year?
I’m not really sure how to answer that. I haven’t paid much attention to it, I suppose.
How have your energy levels been over this past year?
Very low. My wife says I move like I’m walking through deep snow. Getting dressed or even crossing the kitchen takes so long that sometimes I just give up before I’ve done much.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your appetite or weight over this past year?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really kept track of my weight, and I can’t say I’ve noticed any big change in my appetite.
Have you had any trouble concentrating, focusing your thoughts, or making everyday decisions?

Yes. I can’t keep the numbers straight for the senior center budgets anymore. And I’ll sit with a bill or look at the calendar for half an hour, just staring at it, without understanding what I’m supposed to do.
